newsitem.title: FINLAND: SUPPORT STRIKES EXPAND AT ENSO'S PLANTS.
newsitem.headline: SUPPORT STRIKES EXPAND AT ENSO'S PLANTS.

text.p: Workers at forestry group Enso Oy's Imatra mill began a 24-hour sympathy strike early on Tuesday in further support of a strike by workers at a small local paper mill in Kotka, an Enso spokesman said on Tuesday.

Some 1,67 organised workers at Enso's two Imatra mills began the strike after mediation talks between Suomen Kerta Oy and its workers failed again overnight, Enso's personnel manager Seppo Sirkia told Reuters by telephone.
The mills manufacture fine- and laminating papers and paper boards.
On Monday, 450 workers at Enso's Kotka mills were on a 24-hour sympathy strike.
Enso will suffer a total loss of about 50 million markka in turnover as a result of the strikes, Sirkia said.
The Finnish Paper Workers' Union is demanding that the 40 workers at paper napkins, plates and cups manufacturer Suomen Kerta would be covered by the general industry labour market agreement.
The employer side, which does not belong to the employer confederation, wants a local agreement.
The Finnish Forest Industries Federation on Monday filed a motion with the labour court against the Paper Workers' Union in protest against the support strikes.
"These type of strikes should not be allowed -- the law should be changed," Forest Industries Federation's deputy managing director Mauri Moren said on Monday.
Talks between Suomen Kerta and its workers -- who have been on strike since early last week -- are set to resume later on Tuesday.
